rationale: With 'capitalized' set, a candidate has to start with a capital letter. This one does, and is a single deletion from a policy term, so it matches.
The same near miss in lowercase does not match. Requiring a capital is how a name filter avoids firing on ordinary prose, where a fuzzy threshold alone would.
Control: surname/fuzzy-lowercase-near-miss-matches is this text without the option.
A term written exactly, and capitalized, matches with the option on.
An exact policy term in lowercase does not match when 'capitalized' is set.
This is the interaction worth pinning: without the option, matching ignores case, so the same document and the same term give a different answer depending on it.
An implementation applying the capital requirement only to inexact candidates would pass every other case in this file and fail this one.
